sonnet.q1: Only the most recent missed fire time (F_latest) becomes a queued run. The older two get no rows and are dropped. (A skipped row is written for F_latest only if an unfinished run exists.)
sonnet.q2: The tick inserts a `skipped` row for that fire time (since an unfinished run exists), and the new run is not executed. next_fire_at advances to F_next.
sonnet.q3: Up to 3 attempts. After attempt 1 fails: requeued with a 1 minute wait. After attempt 2 fails: 5 minute wait. After attempt 3 fails: run is marked `failed` with finished_at set. Each failed attempt stores its error text on its attempt row.
sonnet.q4: After no heartbeat for 2 minutes the worker is presumed dead; a sweep (run by every worker with the tick) records the attempt as presumed_dead, which counts as a used attempt. The run is then queued with 1 min wait after attempt 1 or 5 min after attempt 2 (counted from sweep detection), so another worker can claim it once next_attempt_at is due. If it was attempt 3, the run is failed; if schedule disabled or tenant paused, cancelled.
sonnet.q5: The running job is left alone and finishes normally. The waiting (queued) run is set to cancelled. The tick makes no new runs while paused. On resume, next_fire_at is recomputed from now (F_next only), so fire times missed during the pause never become runs (no catch-up).
sonnet.q6: The tick selects due schedules with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so two workers never handle the same schedule at once. Also UNIQUE (schedule_id, fire_time) with ON CONFLICT (schedule_id, fire_time) DO NOTHING makes a repeat insert do nothing.
sonnet.q7: In `next_fire_at` (UTC timestamptz) on the JOB_SCHEDULES row. The tick sets it to F_next after handling a due schedule; enabling a schedule or resuming a tenant recomputes it from now (F_next only). The document does not state whether editing the cron expression or timezone changes it, beyond validation when saving.
sonnet.q8: A single SQL statement in one transaction picks one queued run (next_attempt_at <= now(), attempt_count < 3, schedule enabled, tenant not paused) and locks it with FOR UPDATE OF run SKIP LOCKED. It sets status running, bumps attempt_count and fence_token, sets claimed_by and last_heartbeat_at, and inserts the attempt row. Locked rows are skipped by other workers. Only one unfinished run per schedule can exist (partial unique index).
sonnet.q9: In `last_heartbeat_at` on the JOB_RUNS row, written with the database now() every 30 seconds by the working worker. The sweep, run by every worker with the tick, notices rows with status = 'running' and last_heartbeat_at older than 2 minutes.
sonnet.q10: On the run row: status goes back to `queued` and `next_attempt_at` is set (now() + 1 minute after attempt 1, + 5 minutes after attempt 2). The retry starts when a worker claims it through the normal claim step once next_attempt_at <= now(). How often workers run the claim is not decided (open question 6).
sonnet.q11: Once per fire time: a JOB_RUNS row (unique on schedule_id + fire_time). Once per execution try: a JOB_RUN_ATTEMPTS row (unique on run_id + attempt_no, 1 to 3).
sonnet.q12: Fencing: every attempt write filters on its own fence_token and status = 'running'. The takeover bumped the fence token, so the old worker's write matches zero rows and its outcome is discarded. The new worker's outcome stands.
